target.scope: Every line of the report-owned complete paragraph. No fresh alternate-reader or historical sentence-boundary claim.

design.whole_content_draft: An attendant must move himself and three persistent cargo objects to the other bank with a boat carrying him and at most one cargo. Unsafe pairs cannot remain together without him. He takes the middle cargo first, returns alone, takes an outer cargo, brings the middle cargo back, takes the other outer cargo, returns alone, then takes the middle cargo again. All finish safely across. This is an explanation of the solution, not one cargo word per actual voyage.
coupled_claims: The man and boat remain co-located and move together on every voyage.
Only one co-located cargo can accompany him; the same three cargo objects persist.
Unattended W-G and G-C pairs are unsafe at every intermediate state, not merely at the destination.

semantic_consequence.rule: For state positions of M,W,G,C on two shores, every trip flips M and at most one co-located cargo. Forbid W=G!=M and G=C!=M. Start together and finish together on the other shore.
semantic_consequence.interaction: After carrying an outer cargo across, returning alone would leave it with G unattended; G must be brought back. That return is needed because transport capacity and safety are jointly binding.
semantic_consequence.source_path: G, empty, W, G, C, empty, G. The W/C-exchanged solution remains a symmetry. This list is actual source voyages, not target words.
semantic_consequence.target_anchor: f83r.21 contains qokedy otedy before the later chedy. Their prospective reading is a return of G before another C transfer; .22 otedy must keep the same return direction. Clause ownership is still unresolved.
semantic_consequence.source_rival: Exchanging the first and third actual cargo trips preserves counts and final location but leaves G with C unattended immediately.
semantic_consequence.not_new_control: These consequences and the full safe-path count theorem were already established source-only; no replay or target count test was run now.

concrete_rivals: An endpoint-only inventory accepts the unsafe trip exchange.
A cargo list does not require the boat at the loading bank or the necessary return of G.
A custody/loan narrative from RAW372 has different semantic channels: title and obligation do not impose these unattended-pair restrictions.
lexical_syntax_and_source_debts: The story must explicitly bind why things cannot be left together; guessed animal labels alone cannot identify dietary relations.
Wolf/cabbage interchange and shore reversal remain symmetries; natural animal names are not established.
Noun repetitions can be declarations, reasons or actions; no cargo occurrence is automatically counted as a crossing.
All source safety axioms are prospective assumptions: the historical problem states no damage but does not separately print both dietary rules.
No image of a boat or these animals has been identified. Target f83r P3 was previously exposed; no independent confirmation capacity.
Unknown groups must express the initial/final arrangements, empty returns, departure/arrival and reasons. Those statements are not assigned to singleton words here.
